# zlanhs

> Returns the value of the one norm, Frobenius norm, infinity norm, or.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlanhs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlanhs';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlanhs( order, norm, N, A, LDA, WORK ) → number
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>max(N, 1) × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array \| null` | **out** · Input array |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANHS as described above.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANHS is set to zero.
- `A`: The n by n upper Hessenberg matrix A; the part of A below the first sub-diagonal is not referenced.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'`; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: output array

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlanhs.ndarray(
    norm,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → number
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `norm` | `"one-norm" \| "max" \| "inf-norm" \| "frobenius"` | `'max'`, `'one-norm'`, `'inf-norm'`, or `'frobenius'` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>max(N, 1) × N</sub> | Upper Hessenberg matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of A (in complex elements) |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A (in complex elements) |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array` | **out** · Workspace (length >= N, used for inf-norm only, real) |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `norm`: Specifies the value to be returned in ZLANHS as described above.
- `N`: The order of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$. When $N = 0$, ZLANHS is set to zero.
- `A`: The n by n upper Hessenberg matrix A; the part of A below the first sub-diagonal is not referenced.
- `WORK`: where $\mathrm{LWORK} \ge N$ when `NORM = 'I'`; otherwise, `WORK` is not referenced.

</details>

**Returns** `number`: matrix norm value

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "one-norm", "max", "inf-norm", "frobenius"
- `RangeError` second argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

## Notes

-   `zlanhs()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLANHS`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlanhs.f).

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import zlanhs from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlanhs';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const A = new Complex128Array( discreteUniform( 2 * N * N, -10, 10, opts ) );
const WORK = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = zlanhs( 'row-major', 'one-norm', N, A, N, WORK );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = zlanhs.ndarray( 'one-norm', N, A, N, 1, 0, WORK, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLANHS`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLANHS returns the value of the one norm, or the Frobenius norm, or the infinity norm, or the element of largest absolute value of a Hessenberg matrix A.

### Returns

$$
\mathrm{ZLANHS} = \begin{cases} \max (\lvert A(i,j) \rvert) & \text{NORM = 'M' or 'm'} \\ \mathrm{norm1}(A) & \text{NORM = '1', 'O' or 'o'} \\ \mathrm{normI}(A) & \text{NORM = 'I' or 'i'} \\ \mathrm{normF}(A) & \text{NORM = 'F', 'f', 'E' or 'e'} \end{cases}
$$

where norm1 denotes the one norm of a matrix (maximum column sum), normI denotes the infinity norm of a matrix (maximum row sum) and normF denotes the Frobenius norm of a matrix (square root of sum of squares). Note that max(abs(`A(i,j)`)) is not a consistent matrix norm.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
